faq.sub: What restaurateurs ask about the kitchen display in IQ Rest. If your question isn't listed — message us on WhatsApp.

items.q: What statuses do kitchen items have?
items.a: Four statuses: Pending — the order is placed and waiting; Cooking — the dish is being prepared; Ready — ready for pickup; Served — delivered to the guest. Tapping the card advances to the next status, with no menus or confirmations.

items.q: Can I set up several KDS screens in different kitchen stations?
items.a: Yes. One tablet on the hot line, another at the bar, a third at the pastry station — each with its own dish-category filter. All screens stay in sync: a status changed on one updates on the rest.

items.q: What do I run the KDS on — do I need a special tablet?
items.a: The KDS runs in any modern browser. A tablet on a stand at the pass suits a large kitchen; a smartphone works for a small venue. No special hardware or installation required: the device connects with a six-digit code from the dashboard.

items.q: Where do orders on the kitchen screen come from?
items.a: From every source: a guest placing an order through the table QR menu, or a waiter taking it on their own device. Orders reach the KDS automatically, with the table number. No manual re-entry from a POS.

items.q: What does an order card show?
items.a: The dish name, selected options (no onions, well done), the guest's comment, allergens, the status and a timer running since the order was placed. Cards sort by priority: the longer a dish waits, the higher it sits in the column.

items.q: Can cards on the screen be filtered?
items.a: Yes. Two filters: by status (for example, only Pending and Cooking) and by category (drinks to the bar, hot dishes to the kitchen). Settings are saved per device, so each station works with its own set.
